summary.highest_risk: The highest-scored finding so far is the historic eastern Pacific El Niño warmth, with NOAA forecasting a record share of the ocean in marine heatwave conditions, followed by the 2026 Arctic sea-ice minimum and the third-lowest Antarctic winter peak, and crude oil from the grounded tanker Caroline Bezengi reaching Oman's coast.
summary.directional_picture: Coverage is in its first days: these findings come from a global sweep of the last week of news and agency releases, not from the sea-by-sea baseline passes, which begin next. Physical and climate findings dominate the early picture; pollution, fisheries and habitat findings will fill in as the baseline passes run.

cross_cutting.label: Climate signal
cross_cutting.text: Marine heatwave extent, king-tide flooding in South Florida and record-low polar sea ice all point the same way in the same season.

cross_cutting.label: Governance in motion
cross_cutting.text: A NOAA public comment on a Clarion-Clipperton nodule permit and the Nairobi Convention COP12 show seabed and regional-sea governance decisions under way.
